articles.title: 完型 · 不要让体重秤绑架健身目标
articles.context: 作者以自己的健身经历说明：过于频繁称重会让注意力从整体健康转向体重数字，改为每两周称重后，训练目标、营养判断和心理状态都更稳定。语气应亲切、务实，像有经验的人在分享可执行的健身建议。
rows: Weighing yourself regularly is a wonderful way to stay aware of any significant weight fluctuations.
定期称体重，是了解自己是否出现显著体重波动的好方法。
advance
However, when done too often, this habit can sometimes hurt more than it helps.
然而，一旦称得过于频繁，这个习惯有时反而会弊大于利。
contrast
As for me, weighing myself every day caused me to shift my focus from being generally healthy and physically active, to focusing solely on the scale.
就我而言，每天称重使我的注意力从保持整体健康、积极活动，转移到了只盯着体重秤上的数字。
story
That was bad to my overall fitness goals.
这对我的整体健身目标并没有好处。
conclude
I had gained weight in the form of muscle mass, but thinking only of lowering the number on the scale, I altered my training program.
我增加的其实是肌肉重量，可因为一心只想着把体重秤上的数字降下来，我还是改变了训练计划。
contrast
That conflicted with how I needed to train to reach my goals.
这与我为了实现目标本来应该采用的训练方式发生了冲突。
conclude
I also found that weighing myself daily did not provide an accurate depiction of the hard work and progress I was making in the gym.
我还发现，每天称重并不能准确反映我在健身房付出的努力和取得的进步。
explain
It takes about three weeks to a month to notice significant changes in your weight due to altering your training program.
改变训练计划后，大约要三周到一个月，体重才会出现明显变化。
explain
The most immediate changes will be observed in skill level, strength and inches lost.
最先显现出来的变化，往往是在动作水平、力量以及身体围度的缩减上。
emphasize
For these reasons, I stopped weighing myself every day and switched to a bimonthly weighing schedule instead.
基于这些原因，我不再每天称重，而是改为每两周称一次。
action_turn
Since weight loss is not my goal, it is less important for me to track my weight each week.
既然减重并不是我的目标，我也就没必要每周追踪体重。
qualify
Weighing every other week allows me to observe and account for any significant weight changes.
每隔一周称一次，既能让我观察到明显的体重变化，也有时间判断这些变化是怎么来的。
explain
That tells me whether I need to adjust my training program.
这样我就能知道是否需要调整训练计划。
conclude
I use my bimonthly weigh-in results to get information about my nutrition as well.
我也会利用每两周一次的称重结果来了解自己的营养状况。
advance
If my training intensity remains the same, but I'm constantly hungry and dropping weight, this is a sign that I need to increase my daily caloric intake.
如果训练强度没有变化，我却总觉得饿、体重还在下降，那就说明我需要提高每天的热量摄入。
explain
The decision to stop weighing myself every day has done wonders for my overall health, fitness and well-being.
停止每天称重这一决定，让我的整体健康、健身状态和幸福感都大为改善。
emphasize
I'm experiencing increased zeal for working out since I no longer carry the burden of a disappointing morning weigh-in.
自从不再背负“早晨一称体重就失望”的心理负担后，我训练时反而更有热情了。
explain
I've also experienced greater success in achieving my specific fitness goals, because I'm training according to those goals, not the numbers on a scale.
我在实现具体健身目标方面也更成功了，因为现在我的训练依据是目标本身，而不是体重秤上的数字。
conclude
Rather than obsessing over the scale, turn your focus to how you look, feel, how your clothes fit and your overall energy level.
与其执着于体重秤，不如把注意力放在自己的外形和感受、衣服是否合身，以及整体精力状态上。
encourage

articles.title: 阅读 Text 1 · 适度内疚如何促进合作与修复关系
articles.context: 文章重新评价“内疚”这种情绪：适量内疚并非纯粹负担，它能促使人反思错误、修复关系，并在同情心不足时成为合作与分享的另一条心理路径。语气应兼具心理学科普的清晰和对复杂情绪的克制理解。
rows: Unlike so-called basic emotions such as sadness, fear, and anger, guilt emerges a little later, in conjunction with a child's growing grasp of social and moral norms.
与悲伤、恐惧和愤怒这类所谓基本情绪不同，内疚出现得稍晚一些，它伴随着儿童对社会规范和道德规范理解的逐渐加深。
compare
Children aren't born knowing how to say "I'm sorry"; rather, they learn over time that such statements appease parents and friends - and their own consciences.
孩子并不是生来就知道该怎么说“对不起”；他们是在成长过程中逐渐明白，这样的话能安抚父母和朋友，也能让自己的良心得到安宁。
contrast
This is why researchers generally regard so-called moral guilt, in the right amount, to be a good thing.
因此，研究者通常认为，所谓道德性内疚只要程度适当，就是一件好事。
conclude
In the popular imagination, of course, guilt still gets a bad rap.
当然，在大众印象里，内疚依然名声不佳。
advance
It is deeply uncomfortable - it's the emotional equivalent of wearing a jacket weighted with stones.
它让人非常难受，就像在情绪上穿了一件塞满石头的沉重外套。
compare
Yet this understanding is outdated.
然而，这种理解已经过时。
contrast

"There has been a kind of revival or a rethinking about what guilt is and what role guilt can serve," says Amrisha Vaish, a psychology researcher at the University of Virginia, adding that this revival is part of a larger recognition that emotions aren't binary - feelings that may be advantageous in one context may be harmful in another.
弗吉尼亚大学心理学研究者阿姆丽莎·瓦伊什说：“人们正在重新关注、重新思考内疚究竟是什么，以及它能发挥什么作用。”她还指出，这种重新审视属于一种更广泛的认识转变：情绪并非非好即坏；一种感受在某种情境下可能有利，在另一种情境下却可能有害。
explain_quote
Jealousy and anger, for example, may have evolved to alert us to important inequalities.
例如，嫉妒和愤怒可能就是进化出来的警报机制，用来提醒我们注意重要的不平等。
example
Too much happiness can be destructive.
就连幸福过了头，也可能具有破坏性。
emphasize
And guilt, by prompting us to think more deeply about our goodness, can encourage humans to make up for errors and fix relationships.
而内疚会促使我们更深入地反思自己的善恶，从而推动人们弥补过错、修复关系。
explain
Guilt, in other words, can help hold a cooperative species together.
换句话说，内疚能够帮助一个依靠合作生存的物种维系在一起。
conclude
It is a kind of social glue.
它就像一种“社会黏合剂”。
emphasize
Viewed in this light, guilt is an opportunity.
从这个角度看，内疚反而是一种机会。
contrast
Work by Tina Malti, a psychology professor at the University of Toronto, suggests that guilt may compensate for an emotional deficiency.
多伦多大学心理学教授蒂娜·马尔蒂的研究表明，内疚可能会弥补某种情感缺失。
report
In a number of studies, Malti and others have shown that guilt and sympathy may represent different pathways to cooperation and sharing.
在多项研究中，马尔蒂等人发现，内疚和同情心可能代表着通向合作与分享的不同心理路径。
report
Some kids who are low in sympathy may make up for that shortfall by experiencing more guilt, which can rein in their nastier impulses.
有些孩子同情心较弱，却可能因为更容易感到内疚而弥补这种不足；内疚能约束他们那些不那么友善的冲动。
explain
And vice versa: High sympathy can substitute for low guilt.
反过来也一样：较强的同情心也可以弥补较弱的内疚感。
compare
In a 2014 study, for example, Malti looked at 244 children.
例如，在2014年的一项研究中，马尔蒂考察了244名儿童。
example
Using caregiver assessments and the children's self-observations, she rated each child's overall sympathy level and his or her tendency to feel negative emotions after moral transgressions.
她结合照料者的评估和孩子们的自我观察，对每个孩子的总体同情心水平，以及他们在发生道德过错后产生负面情绪的倾向进行了评分。
report
Then the kids were handed chocolate coins, and given a chance to share them with an anonymous child.
随后，孩子们拿到了一些巧克力金币，并有机会把它们分享给一个匿名儿童。
sequence
For the low-sympathy kids, how much they shared appeared to turn on how inclined they were to feel guilty.
对于同情心较弱的孩子来说，他们愿意分享多少，似乎取决于他们有多容易产生内疚感。
explain
The guilt-prone ones shared more, even though they hadn't magically become more sympathetic to the other child's deprivation.
那些更容易内疚的孩子分享得更多，尽管他们并没有神奇地变得更能同情另一个孩子所处的匮乏境况。
contrast
"That's good news," Malti says.
马尔蒂说：“这是个好消息。”
dialogue
"We can be prosocial because we caused harm and we feel regret."
“我们之所以能表现出亲社会行为，可以只是因为自己造成了伤害，并因此感到后悔。”
evaluation_quote

articles.title: 阅读 Text 2 · 森林碳汇为何需要“先减后增”的管理
articles.context: 文章解释森林既是应对气候变化的重要碳汇，也会因干旱、虫害和火灾而失去吸碳能力。加州方案通过疏林、清理灌木和优先处理高风险地区，以短期牺牲部分吸碳能力换取长期森林韧性。语气应稳健、清晰、有政策解释感。
rows: Forests give us shade, quiet and one of the harder challenges in the fight against climate change.
森林为我们提供阴凉与宁静，也给应对气候变化带来了最棘手的挑战之一。
advance
Even as we humans count on forests to soak up a good share of the carbon dioxide we produce, we are threatening their ability to do so.
就在我们指望森林吸收相当一部分人类排放的二氧化碳时，我们却正在损害森林完成这项任务的能力。
contrast
The climate change we are hastening could one day leave us with forests that emit more carbon than they absorb.
我们正在加速的气候变化，有一天可能会让森林排放的碳比它们吸收的还多。
warning
Thankfully, there is a way out of this trap - but it involves striking a subtle balance.
好在，这个困局并非无解，只是需要把握一种微妙的平衡。
contrast
Helping forests flourish as valuable "carbon sinks" long into the future may require reducing their capacity to absorb carbon now.
要让森林在未来很长时间里都能作为宝贵的“碳汇”茁壮存在，可能需要暂时降低它们眼下吸收碳的能力。
explain
California is leading the way, as it does on so many climate efforts, in figuring out the details.
和许多气候行动一样，加州正在率先探索其中的具体做法。
advance
The state's proposed Forest Carbon Plan aims to double efforts to thin out young trees and clear brush in parts of the forest.
加州拟议中的《森林碳计划》准备把部分林区疏伐幼树、清理灌木的力度提高一倍。
report
This temporarily lowers carbon-carrying capacity.
这样做会暂时降低森林承载碳的能力。
qualify
But the remaining trees draw a greater share of the available moisture, so they grow and thrive, restoring the forest's capacity to pull carbon from the air.
但留下的树木能分得更多可用水分，从而生长得更好，并逐步恢复森林从空气中吸收碳的能力。
contrast
Healthy trees are also better able to fend off insects.
健康的树木也更能抵御虫害。
explain
The landscape is rendered less easily burnable.
整个林区也会因此更不容易燃烧。
conclude
Even in the event of a fire, fewer trees are consumed.
即使真的发生火灾，被烧毁的树木也会更少。
conclude
The need for such planning is increasingly urgent.
这种规划正变得越来越紧迫。
emphasize
Already, since 2010, drought and insects have killed over 100 million trees in California, most of them in 2016 alone, and wildfires have burned hundreds of thousands of acres.
自2010年以来，干旱和虫害已经导致加州超过一亿棵树死亡，其中大多数仅在2016年一年内死亡；野火还烧毁了数十万英亩林地。
statistic
California plans to treat 35,000 acres of forest a year by 2020, and 60,000 by 2030 - financed from the proceeds of the state's emissions-permit auctions.
加州计划到2020年每年治理3.5万英亩森林，到2030年提高到6万英亩；资金来自该州排放许可拍卖的收入。
statistic
That's only a small share of the total acreage that could benefit, about half a million acres in all, so it will be vital to prioritize areas at greatest risk of fire or drought.
这只占可能从治理中受益的总面积的一小部分——总计约50万英亩，因此优先处理火灾或干旱风险最高的地区至关重要。
conclude

The strategy also aims to ensure that carbon in woody material removed from the forests is locked away in the form of solid lumber or burned as biofuel in vehicles that would otherwise run on fossil fuels.
这一策略还希望确保，从森林中移出的木质材料里的碳，要么以实木木材的形式被长期固定，要么作为生物燃料供原本会使用化石燃料的车辆燃烧。
explain
New research on transportation biofuels is already under way.
关于交通运输生物燃料的新研究已经展开。
report
State governments are well accustomed to managing forests, but traditionally they've focused on wildlife, watersheds and opportunities for recreation.
州政府早已习惯管理森林，但传统上关注的主要是野生动物、流域以及休闲娱乐机会。
contrast
Only recently have they come to see the vital part forests will have to play in storing carbon.
直到最近，他们才逐渐认识到森林在储存碳方面必须发挥的关键作用。
advance
California's plan, which is expected to be finalized by the governor next year, should serve as a model.
加州的这项计划预计将于明年由州长最终敲定，它应当成为一个范例。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 3 · 美国农业缺工与移民政策困局
articles.context: 文章从美国农场长期缺工切入，说明农业劳动力老龄化、本土工人不愿回流、机械化尚不能覆盖高价值作物，以及H-2A签证程序低效等问题，最后把政策选择概括为“进口食物，还是进口采摘食物的工人”。语气应严谨、有现实压力感。
rows: American farmers have been complaining of labor shortages for several years.
美国农场主多年来一直在抱怨劳动力短缺。
advance
The complaints are unlikely to stop without an overhaul of immigration rules for farm workers.
如果不彻底改革农业工人的移民规则，这些抱怨恐怕不会停止。
conclude
Congress has obstructed efforts to create a more straightforward visa for agricultural workers that would let foreign workers stay longer in the U.S. and change jobs within the industry.
国会一直阻挠建立一种更简便的农业工人签证；这种签证本可以让外国工人在美国停留更久，并在农业内部更换工作。
report
If this doesn't change, American businesses, communities, and consumers will be the losers.
如果这一点不改变，美国企业、社区和消费者都会成为输家。
warning
Perhaps half of U.S. farm laborers are undocumented immigrants.
美国农业劳工中，可能有一半是无证移民。
statistic
As fewer such workers enter the country, the characteristics of the agricultural workforce are changing.
随着进入美国的这类工人减少，农业劳动力的构成也在发生变化。
explain
Today's farm laborers, while still predominantly born in Mexico, are more likely to be settled rather than migrating and more likely to be married than single.
如今的农场劳工虽然仍主要出生于墨西哥，但比过去更可能已经定居而不是四处迁移，也更可能已婚而非单身。
compare
They're also aging.
而且，他们正在变老。
emphasize
At the start of this century, about one-third of crop workers were over the age of 35.
本世纪初，大约三分之一的种植业工人年龄超过35岁。
statistic
Now more than half are.
如今，这一比例已经超过一半。
statistic
And picking crops is hard on older bodies.
而采摘作物对年长者的身体负担很重。
conclude
One oft-debated cure for this labor shortage remains as implausible as it's been all along: Native U.S. workers won't be returning to the farm.
一个经常被讨论的解决办法依然和过去一样不现实：美国本土工人不会重返农场。
contrast
Mechanization isn't the answer, either - not yet, at least.
机械化也不是答案——至少目前还不是。
contrast
Production of corn, cotton, rice, soybeans, and wheat has been largely mechanized, but many high-value, labor-intensive crops, such as strawberries, need labor.
玉米、棉花、水稻、大豆和小麦的生产已经大体实现机械化，但草莓等许多高价值、劳动密集型作物仍然需要大量人工。
explain
Even dairy farms, where robots do a small share of milking, have a long way to go before they're automated.
即便是在已经由机器人承担少量挤奶工作的奶牛场，距离全面自动化也还有很长的路。
qualify
As a result, farms have grown increasingly reliant on temporary guest workers using the H-2A visa to fill the gaps in the workforce.
因此，农场越来越依赖持H-2A签证的临时外籍工人来填补劳动力缺口。
conclude
Starting around 2012, requests for the visas rose sharply; from 2011 to 2016 the number of visas issued more than doubled.
大约从2012年开始，这类签证的申请量迅速上升；2011年至2016年，签发数量增加了一倍多。
statistic
The H-2A visa has no numerical cap, unlike the H-2B visa for nonagricultural work, which is limited to 66,000 a year.
H-2A签证没有数量上限，而用于非农业工作的H-2B签证每年上限为6.6万份。
compare
Even so, employers complain they aren't given all the workers they need.
即便如此，雇主仍抱怨自己得不到所需的全部工人。
contrast
The process is cumbersome, expensive, and unreliable.
这一程序繁琐、昂贵，而且不可靠。
emphasize
One survey found that bureaucratic delays led the average H-2A worker to arrive on the job 22 days late.
一项调查发现，官僚程序造成的延误，使H-2A工人平均晚到岗22天。
report
The shortage is compounded by federal immigration raids, which remove some workers and drive others underground.
联邦政府的移民突击执法进一步加剧了短缺：一些工人被带走，另一些则被迫转入地下。
warning
In a 2012 survey, 71 percent of tree-fruit growers and almost 80 percent of raisin and berry growers said they were short of labor.
2012年的一项调查中，71%的树生水果种植者和近80%的葡萄干及浆果种植者表示劳动力不足。
statistic
Some western farmers have responded by moving operations to Mexico.
一些美国西部农场主的应对方式，是把生产经营迁往墨西哥。
report
From 1998 to 2000, 14.5 percent of the fruit Americans consumed was imported.
1998年至2000年，美国人消费的水果中有14.5%来自进口。
statistic
Little more than a decade later, the share of imports was 25.8 percent.
仅仅十多年后，进口水果的占比就升到了25.8%。
statistic
In effect, the U.S. can import food or it can import the workers who pick it.
归根结底，美国要么进口食物，要么进口负责采摘食物的工人。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 4 · 塑料危机不能只靠个人消费选择
articles.context: 文章质疑把塑料污染责任主要交给个人消费者的做法，认为购物袋、吸管等个人行动容易形成“道德许可”，真正大规模改变行为需要税收、禁令、回收便利等结构性政策，同时仍保留公民推动改革的责任。语气应有公共议题评论的清晰立场，但保持克制。
rows: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Dia Mirza and Adrian Grenier have a message for you: It's easy to beat plastic.
阿诺德·施瓦辛格、迪娅·米尔扎和阿德里安·格雷尼尔想对你说：战胜塑料并不难。
advance

They're part of a bunch of celebrities starring in a new video for World Environment Day - encouraging you, the consumer, to swap out your single-use plastic staples like straws and cutlery to combat the plastics crisis.
他们和一群名人一起出演了世界环境日的新视频，鼓励作为消费者的你，用别的东西替代吸管、餐具等一次性塑料日用品，以应对塑料危机。
explain
The key messages that have been put together for World Environment Day do include a call for governments to enact legislation to curb single-use plastics.
世界环境日汇总的核心信息中，确实包括呼吁各国政府立法限制一次性塑料。
qualify
But the overarching message is directed at individuals.
但贯穿其中的总体信息，主要还是面向个人。
contrast
My concern with leaving it up to the individual, however, is our limited sense of what needs to be achieved.
然而，我担心的是，一旦把这件事主要交给个人，我们对真正需要实现什么的认识就会过于有限。
warning
On their own, taking our own bags to the grocery store or quitting plastic straws, for example, will accomplish little and require very little of us.
比如，仅靠自己带购物袋去超市或不用塑料吸管，能实现的改变其实很少，而我们付出的也几乎微不足道。
example

They could even be detrimental, satisfying a need to have "done our bit" without ever progressing onto bigger, bolder, more effective actions - a kind of "moral licensing" that allays our concerns and stops us doing more and asking more of those in charge.
这些行动甚至可能适得其反：它们满足了我们“已经尽过一份力”的心理需要，却让我们不再迈向更大、更大胆、更有效的行动——这是一种“道德许可”，会缓解我们的不安，也让我们不再多做一步，更少去要求掌权者承担更多责任。
emphasize

While the conversation around our environment and our responsibility toward it remains centered on shopping bags and straws, we're ignoring the balance of power that implies that as "consumers" we must shop sustainably, rather than as "citizens" hold our governments and industries to account to push for real systemic change.
当有关环境以及我们对环境责任的讨论仍围绕购物袋和吸管打转时，我们其实忽视了背后的权力结构：它让我们以“消费者”的身份被要求可持续消费，却没有以“公民”的身份追究政府和企业的责任，推动真正的系统性改变。
contrast
It's important to acknowledge that the environment isn't everyone's priority - or even most people's.
我们必须承认，环境并不是每个人最优先考虑的事情，甚至不是大多数人的首要任务。
qualify
We shouldn't expect it to be.
我们也不该期待人人都把它放在第一位。
conclude

In her latest book, Why Good People Do Bad Environmental Things, Wellesley College professor Elizabeth R. DeSombre argues that the best way to collectively change the behavior of large numbers of people is for the change to be structural.
韦尔斯利学院教授伊丽莎白·R·德松布尔在新书《为什么好人会做出坏的环境行为》中提出，要集体改变大量人群的行为，最有效的办法是让改变具有结构性。
explain
This might mean implementing policy such as a plastic tax that adds a cost to environmentally problematic action, or banning single-use plastics altogether.
这可能意味着实施塑料税，让对环境有问题的行为付出成本；也可能意味着彻底禁止一次性塑料。
example
India has just announced it will "eliminate all single-use plastic in the country by 2022."
印度刚刚宣布，将“在2022年前消除全国所有一次性塑料”。
advance
There are also incentive-based ways of making better environmental choices easier, such as ensuring recycling is at least as easy as trash disposal.
还可以用激励型办法，让更环保的选择变得更容易，比如确保回收至少和丢弃垃圾一样方便。
example
DeSombre isn't saying people should stop caring about the environment.
德松布尔并不是说，人们应该停止关心环境。
qualify
It's just that individual actions are too slow, she says, for that to be the only, or even primary, approach to changing widespread behavior.
她只是认为，个人行动推进得太慢，不能成为改变广泛社会行为的唯一办法，甚至也不该是主要办法。
contrast
None of this is about writing off the individual.
以上这些并不是要否定个人的作用。
qualify
It's just about putting things into perspective.
只是要把个人行动放到恰当的位置上看待。
explain
We don't have time to wait.
我们没有时间继续等待。
emphasize
We need progressive policies that shape collective action (and rein in polluting businesses), alongside engaged citizens pushing for change.
我们需要能够塑造集体行动、约束污染企业的进步政策，也需要积极参与的公民持续推动改变。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Part B · 买房时孩子的意见该有多大分量
articles.context: 文章围绕“买房是否该让孩子参与决策”汇集心理学家、地产经纪、律师和分析师的不同意见：让孩子有参与感有益，但最终决策仍应由成年人根据长期需求和财务现实作出。语气应像生活方式报道，轻松、清晰，人物引语保持自然。
articles.domain: family decision making / real estate / psychology
rows: In choosing a new home, Camille McClain's kids have a single demand: a backyard.
在挑选新家时，卡米尔·麦克莱恩的孩子们只有一个要求：要有后院。
story

McClain's little ones aren't the only kids who have an opinion when it comes to housing, and in many cases youngsters' views weigh heavily on parents' real estate decisions, according to a 2018 Harris Poll survey of more than 2,000 U.S. adults.
麦克莱恩家的孩子并非唯一会对住房发表意见的孩子；2018年哈里斯民调对2000多名美国成年人进行调查后发现，在很多情况下，孩子的看法会对父母的房地产决策产生很大影响。
report

While more families buck an older-generation proclivity to leave kids in the dark about real estate decisions, realty agents and psychologists have mixed views about the financial, personal and long-term effects kids' opinions may have.
越来越多家庭正在打破老一代在房产决策中不让孩子知情的倾向，但房地产经纪人和心理学家对孩子的意见可能带来的财务、个人和长期影响看法不一。
contrast

The idea of involving children in a big decision is a great idea because it can help them feel a sense of control and ownership in what can be an overwhelming process, said Ryan Hooper, clinical psychologist in Chicago.
芝加哥临床心理学家瑞安·胡珀说，让孩子参与一项重大决定是个好主意，因为这能帮助他们在一个可能令人无所适从的过程中获得掌控感和主人翁意识。
explain_quote
"Children may face serious difficulties in coping with significant moves, especially if it removes them from their current school or support system," he said.
他说：“孩子如果面临一次重大变动，在适应过程中可能会遇到严重困难，尤其是当这使他们离开目前的学校或支持体系时。”
dialogue

Greg Jaroszewski, real estate broker with Gagliardo Realty Associates, said he's not convinced that kids should be involved in selecting a home - but their opinions should be considered in regards to proximity to friends and social activities, if possible.
在加利亚多房地产联合公司任经纪人的格雷格·雅罗舍夫斯基说，他不认为孩子该参与选房，但如果可能，也应考虑他们离朋友和社交活动地点有多近。
report
Younger children should feel like they're choosing their home - without actually getting a choice in the matter, said Adam Bailey, real estate attorney based in New York.
纽约房地产律师亚当·贝利说，应该让年幼的孩子感觉自己正在选择新家——实际上却不真正把决定权交给他们。
qualify_quote
Asking them questions about what they like about the backyard of a potential home will make them feel like they're being included in the decision-making process, Bailey said.
贝利说，可以问问他们喜欢备选房屋后院的哪些地方，这会让他们觉得自己被纳入了决策过程。
explain_quote
Many of the aspects of homebuying aren't a consideration for children, said Tracey Hampson, a real estate agent based in Santa Clarita, Calif.
加州圣克拉丽塔的房地产经纪人特蕾西·汉普森说，买房时考虑的很多因素，孩子其实并不会考虑。
report
And placing too much emphasis on their opinions can ruin a fantastic home purchase.
而过分看重他们的意见，可能会毁掉一次原本很棒的购房。
warning
"Speaking with your children before you make a real estate decision is wise, but I wouldn't base the purchasing decision solely on their opinions." Hampson said.
汉普森说：“做房地产决定前和孩子谈一谈是明智的，但我不会仅凭他们的意见决定是否购买。”
dialogue
The other issue is that many children - especially older ones - may base their real estate knowledge on HGTV shows, said Aaron Norris of The Norris Group in Riverside, Calif.
另一个问题是，许多孩子——尤其是年龄较大的孩子——可能会根据HGTV节目来形成自己的房地产认知，来自加州河滨市诺里斯集团的亚伦·诺里斯说。
report
"They love Chip and Joanna Gaines just as much as the rest of us," he said.
他说：“他们和我们其他人一样喜欢奇普和乔安娜·盖恩斯。”
dialogue
"HGTV has seriously changed how people view real estate.
“HGTV已经严重改变了人们看待房地产的方式。
evaluation_quote
It's not shelter, it's a lifestyle.
它不再只是遮风避雨的住所，而是一种生活方式。
explain_quote
With that mindset change come some serious money consequences."
这种观念的变化会带来一些严重的金钱后果。”
warning
Kids tend to get stuck in the features and the immediate benefits to them personally, Norris said.
诺里斯说，孩子往往会执着于房子的具体特点，以及这些特点眼下能给他们个人带来的好处。
report
Parents need to remind their children that their needs and desires may change over time, said Julie Gurner, a real estate analyst with FitSmallBusiness.com.
FitSmallBusiness.com的房地产分析师朱莉·格纳说，父母需要提醒孩子，他们的需要和愿望会随着时间改变。
report
"Their opinions can change tomorrow," Gurner said.
格纳说：“他们的意见明天就可能改变。”
dialogue

"Harsh as it may be to say, that decision should likely not be made contingent on a child's opinions, but rather made for them with great consideration into what home can meet their needs best - and give them an opportunity to customize it a bit and make it their own."
格纳说：“这话虽然很残酷，但这项决定很可能不应取决于孩子的意见，而应由父母替他们作出，并充分考虑怎样的家最能满足孩子的需要，同时给他们一点机会去自行定制，并把它变成自己的家。”
evaluation_quote
This advice is more relevant now than ever before, even as more parents want to embrace the ideas of their children, despite the current housing crunch.
尽管当前的住房紧张，越来越多的父母希望接纳孩子的想法，但这条建议如今比以往任何时候都更切合实际。
conclude

articles.title: 翻译 · 詹姆斯·赫里奥特的写作成功从来不是轻而易举
articles.context: 以英国作家詹姆斯·赫里奥特为例，说明看似自然流畅的文字背后，是长期练习、重写、阅读以及面对失望和拒稿仍坚持不懈的结果。
rows: It is easy to underestimate English writer James Herriot.
人们很容易低估英国作家詹姆斯·赫里奥特。
advance
He had such a pleasant, readable style that one might think that anyone could imitate it.
他的文风如此亲切、易读，以至于人们可能会觉得任何人都能模仿。
explain
How many times have I heard people say, "I could write a book. I just haven't the time."
我不知听过多少次有人说：“我也能写一本书，只是没有时间。”
dialogue
Easily said.
说起来容易。
emphasize
Not so easily done.
做起来却没那么容易。
contrast
James Herriot, contrary to popular opinion, did not find it easy in his early days of, as he put it, "having a go at the writing game".
与普遍看法相反，詹姆斯·赫里奥特早年尝试他所谓的“写作游戏”时，也并不觉得轻松。
contrast
While he obviously had an abundance of natural talent, the final, polished work that he gave to the world was the result of years of practicing, re-writing and reading.
他显然天赋充沛，但最终呈现给世人的那些成熟精炼的作品，却是多年练习、重写和阅读的结果。
explain
Like the majority of authors, he had to suffer many disappointments and rejections along the way, but these made him all the more determined to succeed.
和大多数作家一样，他一路上不得不经受许多失望和拒稿，但这些反而使他更加坚定地要取得成功。
story
Everything he achieved in life was earned the hard way and his success in the literary field was no exception.
他一生中的一切成就都靠艰苦努力赢来，他在文学领域的成功也不例外。
conclude
